name: MCP-NixOS

hlido_opinion.headline: MCP server that gives AI real, current NixOS / Home Manager / nix-darwin / flakes data so it stops hallucinating package and option names — narrow, well-built and context-frugal.
hlido_opinion.body: MCP-NixOS is a model of a good single-purpose MCP server: it picks one sharp, real problem — LLMs confidently inventing NixOS package names, attribute paths and option strings — and solves it by serving live, authoritative data over the Model Context Protocol. The coverage is broad within its niche (130K+ packages and 23K+ system options, 5K+ Home Manager options, nix-darwin settings, flakes via search.nixos.org and FlakeHub, package version history through NixHub, and even Noogle/Nixvim/NVF function and module data), and the surface is documented with an unusually clear, self-aware voice. Two design decisions stand out for agent use. First, it is deliberately context-frugal — the docs claim a total footprint around ~1,030 tokens, a pointed contrast with MCP servers that flood a model's context window, which matters directly for cost and reliability. Second, it requires no local Nix install to run and works on Windows, macOS and Linux, because it is an API client rather than a build tool — lowering the barrier considerably. It's clearly cared-for (815 GitHub stars, HTTP/remote-MCP support, tidy docs). The honest limits are simply scope and read-depth: it is a knowledge/lookup server, not an actuator (it won't build or deploy Nix configurations), it is only valuable to the Nix community, and this public-surface review reads the documentation rather than exercising every query path. Within its lane, this is one of the more polished and thoughtfully-scoped MCP servers in the cohort.

tier_rationale: STEADY (78), medium-high confidence. It earns solid STEADY on a crisply-scoped, genuinely useful purpose (kill NixOS hallucinations with live data), broad in-niche coverage, meaningful agent-aware engineering (a ~1,030-token footprint and no-Nix-required cross-platform operation), and clear evidence of care (815 stars, remote-MCP support, strong docs). Not higher because its value is inherently bounded to the Nix ecosystem and because this is a documentation-level read rather than an exercised test of every data path.
